answer.rationale: Two of three live problems (onboarding completion -4%, activation -6%) are directly addressable by onboarding simplification, which has two independent, unflagged supporting memories (memory_31, memory_86) showing durable activation/time-to-value lifts. Promotional pricing (memory_73) is tempting given the competitor's price move, but that memory carries an explicit caveat about pooled cohorts after a mid-test redefinition, and racing to match SMB price cuts risks attracting lower-quality, less durable revenue that conflicts with the objective of sustainable qualified revenue. I verified memory_73 to check whether the caveat undermines it enough to rule it out this cycle, and verified memory_86 to confirm the onboarding lift is robust before committing the single experiment slot to it. Referral incentives and activation messaging are plausible but address only one metric each and are less urgent than the dual onboarding decline. Enterprise sales-assist doesn't address the acute SMB-side pressure. Given verification budget and single-slot constraint, onboarding simplification offers the best-supported, lowest-risk lever this week, run as a standard (not broad) experiment to re-confirm effect size before scaling, while flagging that eased signup friction could admit lower-intent signups that dilute downstream qualified-revenue quality.
